title: add-nvtx-and-microbench-instrumentation-runtime-profiling
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Improve runtime visibility to guide kernel and scheduling optimizations. This PR adds NVTX ranges around hot code paths, lightweight counters for KV cache and batching events, and a small microbenchmark harness for per-kernel timing. The goal is to make it straightforward to collect consistent traces (NVTX) and microbench results across CI and local perf runs so that we can (1) quantify the impact of scheduling/batching changes, (2) isolate KV-cache related stalls, and (3) validate kernel-level optimizations on different GPU architectures.

What this PR does:
- Adds NVTX ranges for: request dispatch, scheduling decision, continuous-batching loop, kv-cache load/store, attention kernel entry/exit, compilation/kernel-selection hot paths.
- Introduces a microbench harness (runtime/microbench) that can: run model-less synthetic workloads, vary batch/seq patterns, collect per-range timings and counters, and dump CSV/JSON summaries.
- Exposes lightweight atomic counters for batching events (batch_formed, batch_sent, batch_wait_ns), kv-cache hits/misses, and kernel_launch_counts. Counters are available via the /metrics debug endpoint and in the microbench CSV.
- Adds CI job redwood-runtime-perf microbench that runs on push to feature branches (disabled on PRs by default to save CI quota) and a script to aggregate NVTX traces into a timeline used by our perf dashboards.
- Adds documentation and examples under docs/perf/instrumentation.md and examples/microbench/README.md.

Checklist:
- [x] NVTX ranges implemented and gated by runtime flag (RUNTIME_NVTX=1)
- [x] Microbench harness with representative workloads
- [x] Export of counters to debug metrics endpoint
- [x] Unit tests for counter increments and harness correctness
- [x] CI job + dashboard aggregation script

Why not more invasive instrumentation? The initial goal is low overhead for production use: NVTX ranges are no-op when not enabled, counters are atomic increments kept minimal, and the microbench runs are opt-in. This PR avoids deep changes to scheduler logic; instead it provides the data needed for follow-up perf PRs that will modify batching/scheduling policies.

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the NVTX scope boundaries (we intentionally kept ranges coarse to limit overhead) and the microbench synthetic workload parameters (we selected them to approximate average customer sequence/batch distributions; see docs).

review_comments: Diego: Can we avoid NVTX allocations on hot path? Suggest using macros to compile out when not enabled.
Author (Ava): NVTX helper is header-only and uses NVTX ranges only when RUNTIME_NVTX is true; added macros and zero-cost path when disabled.
Priya: The batch_wait_ns counter may overflow in long-running tests; consider using 64-bit atomics.
Author (Ava): switched to 64-bit atomic for wait counters and added tests to validate overflow behavior.
Liam: microbench workloads look good. Add a small test to validate that KV-cache hit/miss counters reflect synthetic access patterns.
Author (Ava): added unit test microbench/test_kv_counters and documented how to reproduce locally.
merge_outcome: merged (squash) after two approvals; microbench CI job marked as optional for PRs
release_notes: Added runtime NVTX instrumentation, batching/KV counters, and a microbenchmark harness to improve profiling and drive future kernel/scheduler optimizations.
notes_for_ops: NVTX and microbenchging are opt-in. To enable NVTX in production debug runs set RUNTIME_NVTX=1 in the runtime config. The microbench job posts CSV artifacts to the perf-dashboard ingestion script (ci/perf/aggregate_traces.py). Beware of CI cost if enabling perf job on all PRs.
